title: 2025-07-15 EU/US data sovereignty & subprocessor clarification - Aurora Retail

Send latest sub-processor map and EU-hosted region list
Schedule infra deep-dive with Aurora cloud team (Priya + Naveen) week of 7/21

Set up test tenant in EU region for pilot (2-week trial)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: 60m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Liam (Aurora Head IT), Sofia (Aurora CISO), Emma (Aurora Legal), Naveen (Aurora Cloud)

Summary (auto-gen): Clarify Redwood's region pinning and data residency guarantees, subprocessor list and cross-border processing behavior, customer-managed key options (BYOK/HSM), and audit/logging capabilities. Agree next steps to share SOC2 and subprocessor documentation and to run an EU-region pilot.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have an hour on the calendar, um, quick intro and then Priya will walk through our region pinning and sub-processor story.
00:08 Liam: Thanks, Jordan. Quick note, we're on tight timeline for our compliance review, so want clarity on data residency and any cross-border processing, also who has access to logs.
00:15 Priya: Great, thanks. I'll start with a high-level: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For hosted we have explicit EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-ish — internal name is eu-1), and you can pin a tenant to a region so inference data stays in that region except for certain cross-border operations which I'll call out.
00:30 Sofia: When you say "stays in that region," do you mean both request payloads and logs? Is there any replication to US for analytics?
00:38 Priya: Good question. By default, logs and metrics for the hosted plane are stored in the same region as the tenant. There are optional downstream analytics services that are US-based — those are opt-in and we can disable them per account. We also provide an EU-only data flow in our Private offering.
00:54 Marco: I'll add — under Dedicated and Private, you can opt for customer-managed VPC peering and we do not egress to our central telemetry pipeline unless you opt in for managed observability.
01:05 Emma: Legally we need to see the sub-processor list and confirm no cross-border transfers without explicit contractual consent. Also curious about subprocessors in the US that might process metadata.
01:15 Jordan: Yep, understood. We'll share our up-to-date sub-processor registry. Quick caveat — some low-level infra components (e.g., global certificate managers, certain CDN edges) may have control plane touches but no customer payload persist. We'll mark those clearly.
01:32 Naveen: For the EU pilot we need BYOK — can you support customer-managed keys in an HSM in the EU region? Can't have keys leaving EU HSM.
01:40 Priya: Short answer, yes. We support KMS integrations and BYOK with region-local HSMs on Private and Dedicated. On hosted we offer a managed KMS by default but can do a BYOK arrangement with a dedicated tenancy and contract. Implementation details differ; we'll share the docs.
01:55 Sofia: Are there any scenarios where KV cache or model state is sent to another region for performance? We want guarantees about model context staying in EU.
02:03 Marco: We do prefix and KV caching to speed up generation. For region-pinned tenants, cache nodes are colocated in the same region; we don't tier caches cross-region unless there's an explicit failover where the fallback model may be in another region, and that only happens if you enable multi-region redundancy.
02:20 Liam: What about backups and snapshots? Some vendors replicate backups offsite for DR and those are often in the US.
02:28 Priya: Backups are region-bound by default for Hosted EU tenants. DR snapshots can be stored in an alternate region if you opt-in; we don't do cross-border DR placement without sign-off.
02:40 Emma: From a DPA perspective, we need specific contract language that says no transfer outside the EU without express approval and list of subprocessors.
02:48 Jordan: We'll provide DPA clause examples, and our legal ops has a standard EU data residency appendix we can send.
02:55 Sofia: Can you tell us about audit logs — retention, who can access them, and if we can restrict access to certain Redwood roles only?
03:03 Marco: Audit logs capture admin actions, model version changes, user-token activity (token creation, role assignment) and are stored with configurable retention. For Private/Dedicated we can offer logs to land in your S3 (or equivalent) bucket in-region. Role-based access controls (RBAC) limit Redwood console access; we also support SSO + SCIM provisioning so you can map groups to Redwood roles.
03:23 Naveen: Which IdPs did you validate? Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace?
03:27 Priya: Okta, Azure AD, and Google are validated. We support SAML and OIDC flows, SSO session timeouts can be tuned. SCIM provisioned users map to RBAC roles.
03:38 Liam: Is there an admin audit trail for SSO/SCIM events? We need to prove provisioning events to auditors.
03:45 Marco: Yes, SCIM provisioning events are included in the audit logs and are exportable to your logging endpoint.
03:52 Emma: Encryption — at rest and in transit, certs, and key ownership?
03:56 Priya: All customer payloads are TLS 1.2+/mTLS optional in dedicated/private. At rest we use AES-256 with KMS-managed keys by default. We support BYOK where you control the key in your HSM (Bring Your Own Key) and Redwood never sees the raw key. For extra assurance we can document the key lifecycle and attest to HSM FIPS levels if needed.
04:18 Sofia: Do you do field-level encryption or tokenization for PII inside prompts? Our legal want to minimize PII entering vendor systems.
04:26 Jordan: We have guidance on prompt redaction and recommend pre-processing PII client-side. Some customers run a pre-filtering proxy in their VPC and only send sanitized prompts. We can help design that.
04:36 Liam: Is metadata like request timing and IPs stored with EU residency?
04:40 Marco: Request metadata is stored with the tenant region. IPs are logged in the audit trail and retained per your configured retention policy in-region for EU tenants.
04:50 Emma: Subprocessors — can you confirm which 3rd parties handle model hosting, telemetry, and backups? We need names and locations.
04:58 Jordan: We'll share the registry but high level: cloud infra provider (EU regions) for compute, a managed KMS provider (if you opt for Redwood-managed keys) — both have EU zones; a metrics/alerting vendor is optional and can be disabled. We'll mark each with purpose and region.
05:15 Naveen: What about cross-border incident response? If there's a security incident, will data be transferred to a US-based response team?
05:22 Priya: Incident response is run from the nearest Redwood on-call team, but for customers with EU-only controls we can limit where forensic copies go and use remote sessions rather than copying data out. We also offer a legal hold workflow and the ability to require that any forensic images be performed in-region by a local partner.
05:40 Sofia: Do you have any certifications around encryption key management? HSM attestations?
05:44 Marco: Our cloud KMS providers publish FIPS and common criteria attestations. For customers requiring FIPS-validated HSMs in their own tenancy (private/dedicated), we can integrate with your HSM and provide attestation artifacts.
05:58 Emma: For the DPA, we will want indemnity around unauthorized transfers — can your legal team look at our redlines?
06:05 Jordan: Absolutely. We'll include a draft DPA and our standard limitation language. You can flag sections and we'll loop in legal to negotiate.
06:13 Liam: Practical question — we have EU-only workloads with a hard stop on any processing outside EU. Can Redwood disable any US failover?
06:20 Priya: Yes. We can configure tenancy to be single-region only, no automatic multi-region failover. That does reduce availability surface — we will show the SLA implications.
06:30 Naveen: For throughput, does single-region pinning increase latency for any global users?
06:34 Marco: Only if your end-users are outside the EU region. The inference runtime remains the same; you get slightly higher latency for cross-border users. We'll show you a perf map during the pilot.
06:45 Sofia: On the subprocessor list, we need to see contract clauses that forbid subcontracting to non-listed parties without notice. Is that in your agreements?
06:53 Jordan: Our subprocessor clause includes a notification period and the ability to object within X days for major changes; we'll surface the exact language.
07:00 Emma: For auditability, can Redwood provide an attestation that EU records haven't been exported? Some vendors provide a monthly export log.
07:08 Marco: We emit export/logging events; we can provide a report or feed showing any data egress events for your tenant. That can be part of a compliance package.
07:18 Liam: Are there any hidden data flows for model telemetry? For example, telemetry used to improve models — how do you segregate customer data?
07:26 Priya: We have strict controls: training datasets don't ingest production prompts. Telemetry is aggregated and scrubbed; for EU customers who require it we can disable telemetry forwarding and keep ops data in-region.
07:38 Sofia: I also want to know who at Redwood can access raw prompts and outputs. Are there console roles or internal operations access?
07:46 Marco: By default, internal ops only have role-based access for customer support. Access is logged and requires Just-In-Time approvals for sensitive data. We can restrict access further in dedicated/private deployments.
07:58 Emma: Can we get a list of Redwood personnel who have decryption/admin privileges? Even if redacted, it helps for our audit.
08:05 Jordan: We'll provide a role-to-responsibility mapping and a list of admin roles; we won't publish personal PII but we can provide role counts and background checks summary.
08:15 Naveen: Network details — egress IP ranges, peering requirements, ports. I need these for our firewall team to approve the pilot.
08:22 Priya: We'll share a network diagram and IP ranges. For VPC peering we use a private peering arrangement, and you'll only need to allow outbound HTTPS to specific egress ranges if it's hosted.
08:34 Liam: For the pilot, how long do you need to provision an EU tenant pinned instance?
08:38 Jordan: We can stand up a trial EU tenant in 48-72 hours once we have the order/PO and confirmation of the network details. If you want Dedicated or Private, provisioning is longer — in the 2-4 week range depending on capacity.
08:52 Emma: Does Redwood allow customer-supplied subprocessor restrictions in the contract? We may need to restrict certain US-based subprocessors.
08:58 Jordan: We can negotiate some restrictions, although certain infra providers are required for compute. We'll mark any required subprocessors and discuss mitigations or private deployment options.
09:10 Sofia: A couple of small details — log retention default is 90 days? Can you extend to 2 years?
09:16 Marco: Default hosted retention is 90 days; we can extend to multi-year in Dedicated/Private or via log archival to your S3 bucket in-region.
09:26 Naveen: About BYOK — if we rotate keys every 90 days, will Redwood's runtime handle re-keying without downtime?
09:32 Priya: We support key rotation with minimal disruption; there is a short window for re-encryption handshake but we've automated it. We'll include the operational playbook.
09:44 Liam: Let's talk cross-border fail-open scenarios — if EU region loses capacity, does traffic route to US? What's the failback policy?
09:52 Marco: Failover is configurable. For strict sovereignty you set strict pinning with no automatic failover; for higher availability you can enable multi-region redundancy with explicit consent. Failback policies are documented.
10:05 Emma: Please highlight any parts of your SOC2 report that touch on vendor management and change management — auditors will want those sections.
10:13 Jordan: Noted, we'll pull relevant pages and annotate them for you.
10:20 Sofia: Can you also confirm whether your EU-hosted model catalog includes any models that were trained on public US data sources that might be considered exportable?
10:29 Priya: Model provenance is tricky. We provide model lineage docs; some community/open models have mixed provenance. For strict requirements we recommend pinning to models we verify to meet EU-only data handling, or using your own on-prem model in Private.
10:44 Naveen: For the pilot we'll need: (1) network diagram and egress IPs, (2) subprocessor list, (3) SOC2/ISO artifacts, (4) test tenant in EU region, (5) draft DPA appendix.
10:55 Jordan: Great, that's in line with our next steps. We'll get those artifacts out this week.
11:05 Emma: One last legal ask — if you are doing any manual review of logs or prompts for quality, we need to be notified and approve scope.
11:12 Marco: Manual reviews are rare and tracked; we can add a requirement for customer approval before any manual exposure of content.
11:20 Liam: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after the infra deep-dive.
11:25 Jordan: Thank you — we'll follow up with the artifacts and set the deep-dive.
12:00 [call ends]
